To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interaction between SK2 and CaM is mediated, in part, by electrostatic interactions between Arg-464 and Arg-467 in SK2 and Glutamate-84 and Glutamate 87 in CaM and that Ca2+-independence of these electrostatic interactions is required for Ca2+-dependent gating.

the interaction between SK channels and calmodulin is required for channel surface expression and that the interaction is mediated in part via electrostatic interactions between positively charged residues in the channel and negatively charged residues in calmodulin.

the binding of calmodulin (CAM) to small conductance Ca2+ activated K+ channels (SCK) is mediated in part through the electrostatic interaction with residues Arg-464, Lys-467, Glu-84, and Glu- 87, and that this interaction is required for surface expression and Ca2+-dependent activation of SCK.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of calmodulin in the regulation of small conductance calcium-activated potassium channels.
the role of calmodulin in the function of small conductance calcium-activated potassium channels.
understanding the mechanisms by which the SK channels are regulated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SK channels require CaM for surface expression and that the interaction between CaM and SK2 channels is Ca2+-independant.
the SK channel is composed of two subunits, a CaM and an SK channel pore-forming subunit that are held together by electrostatic and Ca2+-dependent interactions.
CaM is a necessary component for the surface expression and gating of SK channels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SK2 channel requires Ca2+-bound calmodulin for both surface expression and gating.
the SK channel pore-forming α-subunit is a CaM-binding protein and that the binding of CaM to SK2 is required for channel trafficking and surface expression.

the electrostatic interactions between the channel pore and the CaM binding domain are essential to maintain a Ca2+-dependent interaction between the two subunits that is required for channel expression at the surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SK channels are constitutively associated with Ca2+-CaMs and that this association is required for the channel to be transported to the surface.
the electrostatic interaction is important in Ca2+-dependent activation of SK channels.
Ca2+-independant interactions with CaM is required for surface expression and that constitutive association between CaM and SK2 is not an essential gating mechanism.
